title: Matrix ownership and parallel small teams
subtitle: DMuon‑2 · Parallel Agent Teams · PPO
intro: Two readings examine whole-matrix updates in sharded training and why multiple small teams can beat independent agents or one large team. Briefs cover cooperative training, verifier noise, inference budgets and architecture scaling. The classic develops PPO’s one-sided clipping.

articles.paper: DMuon-2: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership and Communication
articles.authors: Starrick Liu · Ruizhi Chengze · Lufang Chen · Michael Zhao · Ran Yu · Xiaofan Li · Dance Kuzi · Yue Zhang · Zijuan Lin · SongAo Han · YongHua Chen · Ruyi Gan · Hao Wang
articles.title: One owner per matrix, rather than orthogonalizing each shard
articles.dateNote: First posted 11-04 14:43 EST; version read: v2, 11-06 04:14 EST; 2026
articles.evidence: Read design, throughput and numerical-equivalence setup; checked v1 but not all differences, so results are not attributed as new to v2

blocks.text: FSDP/ZeRO shards commute with elementwise AdamW updates, but not generally with matrix orthogonalization. DMuon‑2 gathers each complete matrix to one owner, balances estimated compute, then publishes updates. [1,2]

blocks.label: Exact-polar illustration; implementation uses finite Newton–Schulz and checks correspondence to whole-matrix updates [1]

blocks.text: HSDP shares owners and optimizer state across replicas. Each finished matrix can be published across nodes while later work continues. This reorganizes communication and ownership rather than the optimization objective. [1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: LLM throughput runs use random tokens; VLA uses prepared LIBERO batches and excludes loading. These measure training-step throughput, not time to matched validation loss. [1]

articles.paper: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
articles.authors: Junlin Wang · Haozhe Chen · Ang Li · Rahul Chalamala · Zhuang Liu
articles.title: Collaboration lifts the mean; multiple teams retain selection gains
articles.evidence: Read method, Gaussian-score model and cost accounting; not reproduced

blocks.text: With budget B agents, each running for a fixed duration, k-agent teams provide N=B/k independent samples. Members share findings; a task verifier selects the best submission across teams. [3]

blocks.tex: X_k\sim\mathcal N(\mu_k,\sigma_k^2),\qquad \mathbb E\max_{i\le N}X_{k,i}=\mu_k+\sigma_k a_N,\quad a_N=\mathbb E\max_{i\le N}Z_i
blocks.label: Paper’s statistical model: independent samples, with Zᵢ standard normal; a₁=0 [3]
Large-sample extreme-value approximation, not an accuracy guarantee at N=1 [3]

blocks.text: For Qwen3.8‑27B at B=100, teams of ten beat independent agents on 10/12 long-horizon tasks and beat one team of 100 on all four tested tasks. The Gaussian model predicts the gain’s sign correctly on only 9/12 tasks. [3]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Equal agent-duration budgets do not fix generated tokens or exact FLOPs. GPU-time and API-token dollar accounting are separate; results depend on verifiable submissions and sample diversity. [3]

blocks.text: A two-tier recommendation cascade escalates selected requests to self-consistency, multi-path reasoning or larger models. classic.question: After several minibatch updates, can other samples move a shared-parameter policy farther after one sample reaches a clipping plateau, and how would you diagnose this on the same batch?

blocks.text: TRPO (2015) constrains updates with a KL trust region. PPO (2017) instead uses a first-order objective for repeated minibatch optimization. Sample under fixed old policy π₀ and hold estimated advantages Â fixed during the update round. [11,12]

blocks.tex: r_t(\theta)=\frac{\pi_\theta(a_t\mid s_t)}{\pi_0(a_t\mid s_t)},\qquad L^{\rm CPI}(\theta)=\widehat{\mathbb E}_t[r_t(\theta)\widehat A_t]
blocks.label: Surrogate over old-policy state–action data, not the full current-policy state distribution [11]
Equation 7 takes the smaller term, rather than simply truncating r [11]
Equivalent form: beyond the threshold, increasing good-action probabilities or decreasing bad-action probabilities gives a flat incentive

blocks.tex: L^{\rm CLIP}\le L^{\rm CPI},\qquad \left.\nabla_\theta L^{\rm CLIP}\right|_{\theta=\theta_0}=\left.\nabla_\theta L^{\rm CPI}\right|_{\theta=\theta_0}
blocks.label: Local agreement for ε>0: this lower-bounds the unclipped surrogate, not true policy performance [11]

blocks.tex: L^{\rm total}=\widehat{\mathbb E}_t[\ell(r_t,\widehat A_t)-c_1(V_\theta(s_t)-V_t^{\rm targ})^2+c_2\mathcal H(\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid s_t))]
blocks.label: Equation 9 form for shared networks: policy, value fitting and entropy terms, followed by multiple minibatch epochs [11]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Clipping does not force every ratio inside the interval or imply a KL bound or monotonic improvement. The paper also studies adaptive KL penalties; this note treats the clipped variant. [11]
